name: mcp-bbc-goodfood
description: MCP server for BBC Good Food. Search recipes, read one, and put its ingredients to a number of people. No API key required.
long_description: List the axes a recipe search can be narrowed along on BBC Good Food, with the values each one takes and how many recipes carry them, measured inside one search or across the whole listing. The site accepts any value on a facet and answers one it does not know with a total of zero, so a guessed spelling comes back as a confident absence; publishing the vocabulary is what makes the question askable. Search the site, then read one recipe from the path a row carries: its ingredients, its steps, its times, its rating and its nutrition. A recipe behind the site's subscription comes back without its ingredients and steps, and says so. Ingredients can be put to a different number of people, and every recomputed figure is announced as this server's arithmetic rather than the site's: three eggs halved come back as two, because half an egg is not an amount a kitchen measures out. Read-only, no API key and no account.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: List the axes a recipe search can be narrowed along, with the values each takes and how many recipes carry them.

query.description: A search to measure the counts inside. The site counts its facets over the rows a search returns, so a count without a query describes the whole listing instead.

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.description: Search recipes and return a listing, narrowed by diet, cuisine, meal type, difficulty, a bound, or by leaving out what sits behind the site's subscription.

query.description: A dish, an ingredient, a technique.

sort.description: How the site orders the rows. Default 'relevant'.

min_rating.description: At least this many stars, 1 to 5.

exclude_premium.description: Drop the rows that sit behind the site's subscription. The site offers no such restriction, so the rows are removed from the page after it arrives: a page comes back shorter than the limit asked for, and a short page is not the end of the results.

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Read one recipe: its ingredients, steps, times, rating and nutrition, from the page path a search row carries, in either of the two renditions the site writes.

id.description: The page's own path, as a search_recipes row carries it.

servings.description: Put the ingredients to this many people. Quantities are then recomputed by this server, not published by the site, and each line says so under 'scaling'.

unit_system.description: Which of the site's own two renditions to read: 'metric' as it writes for its own readers, 'us' as it restates for readers in the United States. Both are the site's words. A recipe it restated nowhere comes back as it published it, said in 'unit_system' and in the notes.

tools.name: scale_ingredients
tools.description: Put a list of ingredient lines to a different number of people, with each line saying whether its figure is exact or was moved to stay usable in a kitchen.

ingredients.description: The lines to scale, as a recipe writes them, such as '200g plain flour'.

factor.description: What to multiply every quantity by. Pass this or the servings pair, never both.

from_servings.description: How many people the list feeds as written.

to_servings.description: How many people it should feed.
